notes: Four-lane parallel sweep (ai / bigtech+hardware+mobile / devtools+cloud / security) via background subagents covering 2026-10-12/13. Routine EGRESS_BLOCKED on nearly every org-domain WebFetch; all four lanes worked around it via WebSearch. Oct 12-13 was a quiet same-day announcement window across all lanes except one AI conference (ai-PULSE 2026, today); most forward-looking candidates each lane surfaced were already filed at equal or better confidence, so this run is small and correction-heavy: one confidence upgrade (EU AI Act GPAI deadline, now backed by the regulation's own Article 111 text), one date correction (Apple's Q4 FY2026 earnings moved from Oct 29 to Nov 2 per Apple's own IR page), and six new cloud/devtools lifecycle dates (AWS Lambda Python 3.10 runtime deprecation, Amazon EKS 1.32 extended-support end, Azure Database for PostgreSQL 14 and Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL 14 support end dates, Docker's Content Trust/Notary v1 shutdown, and Docker Hub Automated Builds removal).
concerns: The security lane re-found Let's Encrypt's 64-day default-certificate switch (2027-02-10) under yet another paraphrased title ('Let's Encrypt default certs drop to 64-day lifetime'); data/events/2027-02.json already carries this fact twice — once active ('let-s-encrypt-default-profile-switches-to-64-day-certificate-2027-02') and once status:superseded from a prior run's own near-duplicate mistake. Deliberately not filed a third time. This is the same slug-truncation/title-token-overlap gap in src/lib/id.ts flagged in multiple prior runs' concerns (shared tokens like 'default'+'64'+'day' land under the 0.6 Jaccard floor when the rest of the title is paraphrased) — still unresolved and still catching new runs.

Standing issue, not introduced this run: data/events/2027-01.json still carries three near-duplicate entries for the same Google Play Contacts/Location/SMS policy change, all dated 2027-01-27. This run's lane found that one locale of developer.android.com/distribute/play-policies dates the related geofencing-as-foreground-service removal at 2026-08-26 (already past) while another locale copy says 2027-01-27 (matching the existing cluster) — a genuine locale inconsistency on Google's own page, not just an aggregation gap. Not filed as a fourth entry; a maintainer merging the cluster should resolve which geofencing date is current before folding it in.

The devtools/cloud lane found conflicting official HashiCorp dates for the HCP Vagrant deprecation: HashiCorp's own blog post says the migration deadline is 2026-12-31, but HashiCorp's own docs page (developer.hashicorp.com/hcp/docs/vagrant/hcp-vagrant-eol) gives a different, later timeline (new-box-creation end 2026-12-14, support end 2027-03-15, operations end 2027-06-07). Two primary pages from the same org disagree — not filed per the no-guessing-dates rule; a maintainer with working fetch access to both pages should reconcile which is current before this is added.

The bigtech lane flagged that the already-filed 'EU expected to designate AWS and Microsoft Azure as DMA gatekeepers' (2026-11-01) may be over-precise: the European Commission's own communications only say a 'preliminary view' was issued June 25, 2026 with a final decision 'expected by end of 2026' — no Nov 1 date was found supporting the existing entry. Not changed this run since no better date was found either, just flagging the existing Nov 1 date's precision as unverified.

The security lane cross-checked the already-filed 'CISA links five KEV-catalog flaws to Flax Typhoon, sets Oct 11 federal deadline' and found the exact CVE list disagrees between two independent outlets (thehackernews.com vs. a Greek-language mirror) beyond the one CVE both agree on (CVE-2015-3306, ProFTPD). The Oct 11 deadline itself has also now passed. Left as filed (already 'expected') rather than touched, but a maintainer should verify the full five-CVE list directly against cisa.gov's KEV catalog if fetch access ever works.

Istio 1.30's end-of-life date remains disputed between endoflife.date (~2026-11-30) and endoflife.ai ('expected ~December 2026, pending Istio 1.32') — standing issue from prior runs, still unresolved, still not filed.
